sources.entry: The Ralph Playbook by Clayton Farr - A remarkably detailed and comprehensive guide to the Ralph Wiggum technique, featuring well-written theoretical commentary paired with practical guidelines and advice.

summary.one_liner: A detailed, opinionated guide and set of prompt/script templates for running the "Ralph" technique: an autonomous AI coding agent driven by a simple bash loop that repeatedly feeds it a prompt, with planning and building modes.
summary.what_it_does: The playbook walks through a three-phase workflow (requirements conversation, planning loop, building loop) that turns project ideas into specs under specs/, an IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md task list, and iterative commits. It documents the core loop mechanism: a bash script restarts a fresh Claude session per task, with the plan file on disk as shared state between iterations. It includes template PROMPT_plan.md and PROMPT_build.md files, an AGENTS.md guide for build/test commands that provide backpressure, and an enhanced loop.sh with plan/build mode selection and max-iteration limits. It also covers context-window management via subagents, sandboxing advice for running with permissions skipped, and several proposed enhancements (interview-driven planning, acceptance-driven tests, LLM-as-judge backpressure, and scoped work-branch planning). A streamed-output variant of the loop script is also included.
use_cases: Run an autonomous coding agent in a loop to implement a spec-driven project
Structure requirements into specs and a prioritized implementation plan for AI agents
Set up backpressure with tests and build commands for unattended AI coding
Write a bash loop script that restarts Claude Code per task
Plan scoped AI-driven work on separate git branches
Sandbox an autonomous agent that runs with permissions skipped
notable: Two-prompt design (PLANNING vs BUILDING) run through the same bash loop, with the plan file as persistent state between fresh sessions
Emphasis on backpressure: AGENTS.md wires project-specific test/typecheck/lint commands into each iteration
Explicit sandboxing guidance for running with --dangerously-skip-permissions
Includes a full enhanced loop.sh and a streamed-output variant contributed by community members
Proposed enhancements such as acceptance-driven tests and LLM-as-judge review for subjective criteria, which the author labels as still being evaluated
caveats: Relies on the Claude CLI with --dangerously-skip-permissions; the README says a sandbox is the only security boundary
Several enhancements are explicitly marked as still being determined in value and viability
Templates assume Claude subagent naming; other CLIs (amp, codex, opencode) are mentioned only as drop-in alternatives for the basic loop
keywords: automate coding with ai in a loop
